archetypes.name: decision-conflict
archetypes.rationale: DECISION_1 was a 2-1 split with the dissenting judge citing closed issue #2756 as the binding Codex-first contract — this archetype hunts for all landed decisions this plan silently contradicts without a blocking operator gate
archetypes.prompt_body: Read SECURITY.md L106, scripts/test-implement-step2-routing.sh L31-32, and any commit messages or issue cross-references mentioning #2756 to establish what the landed Codex-first product decision actually says and whether it was explicitly closed as a permanent contract or a provisional default. Determine whether the plan's Gate C callout is a genuinely blocking gate (operator must revise the plan before implementation proceeds) or advisory prose that an automated runner could silently skip, and flag the difference. Check whether any other sections of SKILL.md, implement-bootstrap.md, or docs/ also encode the Codex-first order in a way the plan does not enumerate for update. Verify that the SECURITY.md adjacency sentence the plan adds accurately characterizes #2756 as reversed-by-#2738 rather than superseded, and that no other closed [DONE] issues are contradicted by the plan without a parallel Gate callout. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: deletion-completeness
archetypes.rationale: Mass deletion of ~576 SKILL.md lines and four named sub-sections creates cross-reference rot risk; the plan enumerates only six files to update but heading strings and semantic content may survive in docs/, agents/, hooks/, or other skills
archetypes.prompt_body: For each section heading the plan marks for deletion from skills/implement/SKILL.md (### Step 0 — tracking issue adoption, ### Larch-log Batches and Summary Comments, ### Plan materialization from issue body, ### Implementer waterfall), search the repo for references to those exact strings and compare found locations against the plan's file list to surface any missed update sites in docs/, README.md, agents/, or .claude/rules/. Verify that the single-fence collapse correctly satisfies the BASH_AUTHORING.md §4 lint contract: the per-anchor comment string the plan proposes (# Foreground required: see BASH_AUTHORING.md §4) is not the normative string in §4 (# Background pair required: see BASH_AUTHORING.md §4), so check whether lint-foreground-markers.sh would accept the proposed string or reject the fence. Check whether the plan's instruction to keep a single CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT recovery line at the top of the collapsed fence is explicit enough — the current multiple-fence boilerplate pattern may be referenced by dirty-tree recovery prose in docs/workflow-lifecycle.md or similar that would also need updating. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
